closed-mode-create-a-closed-datum-regist.text: Closed mode: create a closed-datum registry, and refuse an update on it.

The release archive carries the open-datum application and, once issue 651 lands, a closed-datum entry point in the same program: the payload of a name is written once at registration and every update is refused on chain. A person cannot yet choose it. This ticket gives the open-datum executable the choice at create and teaches every later command to follow the registry's mode, with no further flag. It is the executable half of issue 650. Issue 654.

story.text: As the presenter of Demo 1, I type open-datum create --closed from the release and get a registry whose application is closed-datum. Every later open-datum command (insert, inspect, terminate, fold) follows that registry's mode with no further flag, and open-datum update on it stops before anything is built or signed, with a plain message saying the registry is closed. Without --closed, every command behaves exactly as today.

What the presenter sees: the create receipt names the application open_datum.closed_datum and prints its pin; an insert, a fold, a termination and an inspect on that registry work as they do on an open one; an update prints that the registry is closed and exits with the client-refusal status, having read no key and built no transaction. The scene is rehearsed on Saturday 17 October.

what-is-established.text: Read on main at cfe78df1 on 15 October 2026. Each statement below was checked against the source before the plan relied on it.

The open-datum value is one constant, openDatumApplication, pinned by the title open_datum.open_datum. The title is read in exactly two places: the release loader, which extracts that title's code from the blueprint (offchain/cli/src/Singular/CLI/Registry.hs, the PinByScript case), and the create receipt, which prints it as application (offchain/cli/src/Singular/CLI/Create.hs, pinApplicationName).

Every command loads its release through the environment's loader, envLoadRelease env app blueprint: create (Create.hs), inspect (Inspect.hs), the booking precheck (Booking.hs), the attached write (Attached.hs) and the preview (Preview.hs). The loader is a field of the environment record, so one command can be run with a different loader without editing any module that calls it.

The registry resolution (resolveRegistry) derives the application policy from the code the loaded release carries, applied to the registry identity, and refuses registry-pin-mismatch application when the state datum records another policy. The title inside the application value plays no part in that derivation. A command that loads the wrong mode's code therefore cannot build against the wrong script: it stops at that named refusal.
The state datum records the application hash (application_policy). The state output is found from the state token alone (findStateOutput), so the mode is readable from the chain with no local file.

The shared flag reader refuses a switch it does not know ("is not a flag singular reads"), and the singular binary reads the same shared list. Adding --closed to the shared list would change singular commands.

The wallet-preparation work (issue 491) edits the open-datum Entry.hs, Plan.hs, Preview.hs and WalletShortfallSpec.hs, and the registry command line's Prepare.hs, Plan.hs and CommandRunSpec.hs. Its two open branches were read on 15 October 2026 (feat/491-prepare-application at 0d1d184e): they change no file this ticket changes.

requirements.text: closed-switch-at-create-only: open-datum create accepts --closed, also together with --preview. Every other command, help aside, refuses it by name before anything is read, saying that a registry's mode is chosen at create and read from the chain by every later command. A key whose text is --closed is a key, not the switch. The registry's own singular commands still refuse --closed as an unknown flag.

closed-create-pins-closed-datum: create --closed loads the closed-datum code, pins it, and its receipt names the application open_datum.closed_datum. Without the switch the value, the title and the receipt are the ones of today.

mode-read-from-the-chain: the mode is the one whose application, applied to the registry identity, hashes to the policy recorded in the registry's state datum. It is read from the chain through the state token and never from a file.

unreadable-or-unrecognised-mode-is-not-guessed: a recorded policy that is neither mode's derivation, and a missing or unreadable state, are named refusals of the mode read. The command then runs exactly as it does today, so the registry's own refusal (registry-pin-mismatch application, state-output-missing, and the others) is what the person sees. For each of the two cases the command ends in that named refusal, nothing is built or signed before it, and the command does not ask for the closed-datum code after the mode read.

later-commands-follow-the-registry: for insert, terminate, fold and inspect, the release the command loads carries the code of the registry's mode: the closed-datum code for a closed registry, the open-datum code for an open one. No flag is read.

loader-decides-the-code: the application value that Entry.hs passes still carries the open title when the closed code is loaded. This is stated and guarded: the title does not choose the code, the loader does, and a resolution of a closed registry through that value succeeds.

update-on-a-closed-registry-stops-before-building: update, and update --preview, on a closed registry stop before the release code is used to build, before any signing key is read and before anything is submitted. The message says the registry is closed and that a payload is written once. The outcome class is the client refusal, exit status 10.

open-registries-behave-as-today: on a registry whose recorded policy is the open-datum derivation, and without --closed, every command reads, builds and prints what it does today. The existing suites pass unchanged except for the constructor arity named in the touch list.

help-and-pages-carry-the-switch: the command help, onchain-release/DEMO1.md and the settings table of docs/singular-node.md say what --closed does, and the documented-flags check accepts them. Every changed page keeps its speech and its narration clips, regenerated with the tools.
no-lean-statement: by operator ruling the write-once rule has no Lean statement (see below). Nothing here claims otherwise.

registry-and-fences-untouched: no change to the registry library, the singular commands, the registry command line, the on-chain code, or the files the wallet-preparation work and the signing work are changing.
nothing-on-preprod: no test or command of this ticket reaches preprod.

rulings-in-force.text: Recorded in the words they were given. The first two are the same rulings that bound issue 651 (see its ruling page).

No Lean (operator, 15 October 2026): "We do not need lean here. This is just for demo one, and then we decide if to formalize it." The affected story is the presenter's closed registration. The ruling declares a limit: the write-once rule has no Lean statement, theorem, corpus row or simulator case. It does not change any Lean statement about the registry or open-datum, and it does not permit a rule that contradicts clear Lean: the closed-datum validator reaches every other rule by calling open-datum's handlers.

One application, one flag (operator, 15 October 2026): "make sure you refactor the open datum application enough so that closed datum is just a flag over it." In this ticket the flag is the mode of one application value: the closed value is the open one with a different pin title, and nothing else differs.

On chain (desk and epic owner, 15 October 2026): validator closed_datum is appended inside open_datum.ak with blueprint titles open_datum.closed_datum.{mint,spend,else}; open-datum's hash does not move. Issue 651 delivers it; this ticket consumes it.
The mode comes from the chain (operator, 6 October 2026, users have only a page and the chain): no local file decides it.
Required checks (operator, 14 October 2026): a published check is required by default, and a new hosted job name goes into ruleset 22633401 in the same change. This ticket adds no job name.
Nothing on preprod. Scene 5 on preprod with a closed registry is a separate decision of the operator.

decisions-and-what-they-were-chosen-over.text: Decisions and what they were chosen over.

stated-limits.text: The write-once rule has no Lean statement, by ruling.

The real blueprint's closed-datum title is consumed only by the next ticket of issue 650 (the devnet journey from the release archive). The unit tests here load toy programs under both titles, so they prove which title is requested, not that a release carries it.
A closed registry is read by singular registry describe through the pin in its state datum, as any registry is; the journey ticket exercises that page.
The node's refusal of a crafted update is the last ticket of issue 650.
